description.narrative:
The overall goal is to strengthen the capacity and coordination of the women's movement in Rwanda for more strategic interventions to enhance women's voice and participation, freedom from violence and full enjoyment of human rights.
This goal is aimed to be achieved through the following pathways:
Objective 1: Partners organisations are stronger, more effective and work more strategically and collaboratively
Objective 2: Improved protection from gender based violence with a specific focus on prevention
Objective 3: Rights holders and duty bearers have an increased understanding and respect for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR)
Objective 4: Enhanced qualitative participation of women in decision making and conflict resolution.

Det övergripande målet för insatsen är att bidra till att stärka kvinnorörelsens kapacitet i Rwanda för mer strategiskt arbete för att förbättra kvinnors röst och deltagande, frihet från våld och fulla åtnjutande av mänskliga rättigheter.
Kvinna till Kvinna har verkat i Rwanda sedan 2017, då ambassaden beslutade att finansiera Kvinna till Kvinnas första landprogram i Rwanda. Programmets övergripande mål har varit att bidra till en starkare och mer samverkande kvinnorättighetsrörelse i Rwanda samt att arbeta mer effektivt för jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt. Det nya programförslaget för 2021 - 2024 bygger på framgångar, utmaningar och lärdomar från den nuvarande fasen, samtidigt som fokus flyttas för att svara på socioekonomisk och politisk utveckling för att bättre svara på kvinnors och flickors behov. Insatsen är strukturerat som ett programstöd med två delar. I den första delen vidarebefordras medel till partnerorganisationer för att genomföra sina egna aktiviteter. I den andra delen genomför Kvinna till Kvinna aktiviteter för att öka deras partners totala kapacitet som kvinnorättighetsorganisationer och för att höja deras förmåga att samordna och driva den nationella dialogen.
Programmet delas in i fyra huvudmål:
- Partners är starkare, effektivare och arbetar mer strategiskt och samarbete - Förbättrat skydd mot könsbaserat våld med särskilt fokus på förebyggande - Rättighetsinnehavare och ansvarsbärare (duty bearers) har ökad förståelse och respekt för sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) - Förbättrat kvalitativt deltagande av kvinnor i beslutsfattande och konfliktlösning.

The overarching objective of the intervention is to contribute to strengthen the capacity and coordination of the women’s movement in Rwanda for more strategic interventions to enhance women’s voice and participation, freedom from violence and full enjoyment of human rights.
Kvinna till Kvinna has operated in Rwanda since 2017, when the Embassy decided to fund Kvinna till Kvinna’s first country programme in Rwanda. The overall aim of the programme has been to contribute towards a stronger and more connected women’s rights movement in Rwanda, working more effectively for gender equality and women’s empowerment. The new Kvinna till Kvinna’s proposal for 2021 – 2024 builds on the successes, challenges and lessons learned under the current phase while at the same time shifting the focus of the program to respond to socio-economic and political developments and emerging priorities to better respond to the needs of women and girls. The contribution is structured as a programme support with two pillars. The first pillar, which represents the majority of the programmes funding, is forwarded to partner organizations to implement their own activities. In the second pillar, Kvinna till Kvinna itself implement activities to increase their partners overall capacity as women’s rights organizations as well as their capacity to coordinate and pursue advocacy and national dialogue.
The key impact objectives are: - Partners are stronger, more effective and work more strategically - Improved protection from gender-based violence with a specific focus on prevention - Rights holders and duty bearers have an increased understanding and respect for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) - Enhanced qualitative participation of women in decision making and conflict resolution.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency Sida, and Kvinna till Kvinna Foundation regarding Working together to reinforce change for the respect of women's rights in Rwanda 'Dufatanye', 2021-2024
Kvinna till Kvinna Rwanda phase II

description.narrative:
Results under objective 1 : Partners are Stronger, More Effective and Work More Strategically and Collaboratively.
All 15 partner organisations are working under the strategic plans that aligns with Kvinna till Kvinna's global strategy.
The four new partners that were on boarded in 2023 Impanuro Girls Initiative, Afro Ark, Feminists in Action Development Ambition and Strive for Inclusion underwent through organisational self assessments with an overall average score of 2.96 out of 5. This was a remarkable achievement as the results from this self assessment and the respective scores will be used as baselines to identify areas of development. including strengthening of financial management.
The program named Dufatanye (Meaning Working together in Kinyarwanda) also managed to enable partner organisation's their staff to participate in various networking events that were meaningful and beneficial to the capacity development. Fourteen partners participated in a Gender Based Violence exchange workshop and Two partners were facilitated in attending the Africa Commission on Human and People's Rights NGO forum in Banjul Gambia.
Results under Objective 2: Improved protection from gender based violence with a specific focus on prevention.
In 2023, Partners such as Rwanda Women's Network and Association of Kigali Women in Sport (AKWOS) enhanced community activism by empowering rights holders with training on GBV. As a result, trained rights holders conducted community sensitization initiatives, disseminating information on GBV laws and underlying norms. RWN, leveraged on its rights holders i.e. Women Safe Space Facilitators and Girl Champions, reached 6,323 people. Similarly, AKWOS, through its Women Peace Club members reached an additional 3,026 people.
Results Under Objective 3: Rights holders and duty bearers have an increased understanding and respect for SRHR.
In 2023, Kvinna till Kvinna provided technical support to ten implementing partner organisations that work on SRHR where they strengthening their programs. KtK reviewed the SRHR modules of five of the training modules used by eight partner organisations and provided feedback to POs to integrate all components of CSE including access to contraceptives, safe abortion abortion and others. We noticed gaps around information on contraceptives and STIs we advised FADA to establish a partnership with a health center or a hospital to provide a nurse or a medical practitioner to deliver this kind of session from a medical point of view to avoid myths and misconceptions to which FADA has considered in their following sessions.
In addition to the above, under this outcome, ten partner organisations, specifically (Haguruka, Rwanda Women's Network ,ER, PCR, Rwanda National Association Deaf Women, Save Generations Organisation, FADA, Impanuro Girls Initiative, Afro Ark and FCLLO) have continued to include comprehensive sexuality education to their content in their SRHR program including contraceptive access information on safe abortion including the ministerial order on safe abortion. It can also be noted that some of these organisations, especially the ones established many years ago had not fully embraced these ideals of SRHR. However, through KtK's intervention, there is a tremendous shift that seems to change the misconceptions around this topical issue.
Results under Objective 4 : Enhanced qualitative participation of women in decision making and conflict resolution.
All fifteen implementing partner organisations and their staff participated in the Alliance building workshop themed building local constituency and activism. Participants shared that they learned the meaning of constituency and how to organise at the community level for advocacy. Participants also gained knowledge about inclusion and leaving no one behind in this journey to ensure that their work is responding to the needs of each rights holder.
Generally.
The program Dufatanye, implemented by Kvinna Till Kvinna and her partners, has effectively strengthened women led and feminist organisations through tailored training sessions and strategic development initiatives. Partners have significantly advanced in organisational leadership, policy development, and advocacy efforts, fostering enhanced community engagement and increased participation of women in various initiatives. Additionally, the program's profound impact on the target population, fostering resilience, sustainable development, and transformative change within families and communities is emphasized.
In terms of outreach it is noted that the program extended its reach across all Rwandan provinces, involving a wide range of stakeholders. In total, 2573 duty bearers participated in SRHR activities and 4774 of them were reached by sensitization activities regarding GBV, including policy and legislation, and underlying norms impacting these two distinct topical issues in the gender equality and women empowerment landscape in Rwanda. This is truly commendable of Kvinna til Kvinna that has grown tremendously and gained recognition within the gender equality and women empowerment space over the years.
